letters.title: Hi Pooks!
content: Pedro my love,

I've been trying to figure out a way to keep giving you letters for the time being when I can't send them to you the way I originally planned. And so here we are. I'll keep all the handwritten letters safe and sound until I have the chance to give them to you.

For now, though, I'll type them out for you here on occasion so you can still read them more or less around the time I wrote them. I've been working on this since the start of my winter break, and the whole time I was kind of dying to show you. I had to learn how to code from scratch so I could make this perfect. It's taken endless amounts of videos, help from friends, and getting quite frustrated,but it's still not there yet. I might make tweaks occasionally as my coding improves too. But for now, it'll do what it's intended for.

Regardless, pooks, I just wanted to tell you some important things: You've become the best part of my day. You mean the world to me, and I really wanted to find a way to show you how important you are. I know I'm not always great with words, but here I'll have time to think of what to say, so hopefully you'll understand just how much I care about you. I know I always joke that I'm this strong, independent woman, and truth be told, I think I am to some extent. I can stand on my own, and I don't mind being alone, but I don't want to be. I want to spend my life with you.

You've become the best thing about waking up in the morning and the person I dream of at night. You're my best friend, the one person I wanna tell everything to and the first person I want to call whenever I get news, both good or bad. You make my heart happy. I love you, Pedro, and I can't wait to spend the rest of my life with you.

letters.title: I miss you.
content: Pedro my love,

Truth be told, I always thought long-distance was such a stupid thing to do. It’s like punishing yourself for loving someone. And I still think it’s the worst punishment you can make someone endure. Some days, it feels especially heavy.

The past few days have been a little bit hard. Not just because of everything that has happened, but because I’ve never wanted you here with me as much as I did when I was sitting in the doctor’s office alone. It sounds silly, and maybe a bit selfish, but I just really wanted to have your hand to hold. I wanted you beside me.

And I think going through tough things nowadays really makes me notice just how much I value you. Because even when you can’t physically be here, you’re always there in every other way. You help carry the mental load. You listen, you check in, you make things feel a little less overwhelming. You already take such good care of me, and I honestly don’t know what I would do without you.
Pooks, you make me feel so incredibly loved. I wish you knew how much you mean to me.
And maybe that’s why, while I was waiting for you to get home the other night, missing you like I always do, I found myself thinking about us and about how certain I feel that we’ll be okay.

I know you’re not the religious type, but I was reading my Bible while I waited for you, and I came across this verse: Truly I tell you that if two of you agree on anything you ask for, it will be done by my Father in heaven. Matthew 18:19.

And, well, Pooks, I know you’re the love of my life, and I’ve heard you say the same thing to me. So I have faith in us. I have faith that, no matter how difficult this distance feels sometimes, you and I will get through it. And one day, all of this missing each other will just be something we look back on.
Because I really do believe that you and I are going to build a wonderful little life together.

And maybe that’s one of the things I love most about you. It isn’t only the big things. There are so many small things about you that I’ve noticed recently, little things that remind me just how deeply you love me.

Sometimes your love is loud and wonderful, like when you make me laugh, pull silly faces for the camera, or randomly tell me how much you love me. Other times, though, you carry the weight in ways I sometimes miss. Like when you call me even after you’ve had the longest day, or when you check in on me when I get quiet.
Those things might seem small, but they really aren’t.
You make me feel wanted. You make me feel safe. You make me feel loved, even from so far away.
And I’m sorry if I don’t always recognize everything you do for me, love. I hope you know that I notice more than I probably say. You do all these small things that actually aren’t small at all.

I miss you terribly, Pooks. But more than that, I’m grateful for you. And even on the days when I wish more than anything that you were here beside me, I remind myself that being apart doesn’t mean being alone.
I have you. And I’m so lucky that I do.
